@@ -55,0 +60,27 @@
+ * @build WallClock
+ *
+ * @comment Why do we configure `sun.net.httpserver.clockTick`?
+ *
+ *          Right after the server detects the socket is readable (e.g.,
+ *          write/close by the client) the server's connection state switches
+ *          from `NEWLY_ACCEPTED` to `REQUEST`, and the request timeout
+ *          mechanism gets armed. This implies a "pause at the beginning of the
+ *          request line" can go unnoticed in the `NEWLY_ACCEPTED` state. This
+ *          test verifies that behavior. But there is a corner case, which can
+ *          still evict the connection.
+ *
+ *          The connection idle timeout in the `NEWLY_ACCEPTED` state is
+ *          configured as `min(IDLE_INTERVAL, MAX_REQ_TIME)`. That is,
+ *          effectively, the idle timeout during `NEWLY_ACCEPTED` will always be
+ *          3 seconds for this particular test, since `IDLE_INTERVAL` defaults
+ *          to 30 seconds. As a result, an idle connection scan can hit our
+ *          connection at `NEWLY_ACCEPTED` and evict it unexpectedly. To avoid
+ *          this corner case, we effectively disable idle connection scan by
+ *          setting is run frequency, determined by
+ *          `sun.net.httpserver.clockTick`, to an excessive value, 1234567.
+ *
+ * @comment Why do we configure `sun.net.httpserver.timerMillis`?
+ *
+ *          It determines the frequency the timeout check mechanism is
+ *          triggered. We up its pace to increase the timeout check
+ *          responsiveness.
@@ -56,3 +88,0 @@
- * @comment `sun.net.httpserver.timerMillis` determines the frequency the
- *          timeout check mechanism is triggered. Up its pace to increase
- *          the timeout check responsiveness.
@@ -60,0 +89,1 @@
+ *      -Dsun.net.httpserver.clockTick=1234567
@@ -96,0 +126,17 @@
+    // Verify the provided time configuration
+    static {
+        long maxReqDurationSecs = Long.getLong("sun.net.httpserver.maxReqTime", -1);
+        assertNotEquals(
+                -1, maxReqDurationSecs,
+                "`sun.net.httpserver.maxReqTime` is not configured");
+        Duration maxReqDuration = Duration.ofSeconds(maxReqDurationSecs);
+        assertTrue(
+                TOLERATED_PAUSE_DURATION.compareTo(maxReqDuration) < 0,
+                "Tolerated pause duration (%s) must be shorter than the maximum request time (%s)"
+                        .formatted(TOLERATED_PAUSE_DURATION, maxReqDuration));
+        assertTrue(
+                EXCESSIVE_PAUSE_DURATION.compareTo(maxReqDuration) > 0,
+                "Excessive pause duration (%s) must be longer than the maximum request time (%s)"
+                        .formatted(EXCESSIVE_PAUSE_DURATION, maxReqDuration));
+    }
+

See the GNU General Public License + * version 2 for more details (a copy is included in the LICENSE file that + * accompanied this code). + * + * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License version + * 2 along with this work; if not, write to the Free Software Foundation, + * Inc., 51 Franklin St, Fifth Floor, Boston, MA 02110-1301 USA. + * + * Please contact Oracle, 500 Oracle Parkway, Redwood Shores, CA 94065 USA + * or visit www.oracle.com if you need additional information or have any + * questions. + */ + +import java.time.Duration; + +/** + * Utilities using system's wall clock. + */ +public final class WallClock { + + private WallClock() {} + + /** + * The sleep duration in a busy loop. + */ + private static final long BUSY_LOOP_PAUSE_DURATION = 10; + + /** + * Sleep for the specified duration using the system's wall clock time. + *

+ * A backward clock adjustment extends the wait; a forward adjustment can + * shorten it in monotonic elapsed time. + * + * @implNote + * The sleep has a busy loop of {@value #BUSY_LOOP_PAUSE_DURATION} milliseconds. + * Durations lower than this can unexpectedly wait longer. + */ + public static void sleep(Duration duration) { + sleep(duration.toMillis()); + } + + /** + * Sleep for the specified duration using the system's wall clock time. + *

+ * A backward clock adjustment extends the wait; a forward adjustment can + * shorten it in monotonic elapsed time. + * + * @implNote + * The sleep has a busy loop of {@value #BUSY_LOOP_PAUSE_DURATION} milliseconds. + * Durations lower than this can unexpectedly wait longer. + */ + public static void sleep(long durationMillis) { + long startInstantMillis = System.currentTimeMillis(); + while (System.currentTimeMillis() - startInstantMillis < durationMillis) { + try { + Thread.sleep(BUSY_LOOP_PAUSE_DURATION); + } catch (InterruptedException _) { + // Restore the interrupt + Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); + throw new RuntimeException("Interrupted!"); + } + } + } + +}
